sections.h2: Who to call about a Haywood County tax bill
sections.html:
Haywood's tax work is divided between two counters inside the Historic Haywood Courthouse, 215 N. Main Street, Waynesville. Values come from the assessor in Suite 220. Bills and payments run through Collections in Suite 224.

Collections, at 828-452-6643, handles partial payments and payoff figures for a parcel that is being sold. The assessor's reappraisal line is 828-452-6734.

The county rate is not the whole bill. The county collects for 22 fire districts, 10 road maintenance districts and one sanitation district. Owners of improved property, manufactured homes and campers included, also pay a landfill fee.

The July 2025 population estimate is about 63,369, a gain of 2.1% over 2020. Of 36,637 housing units, 74.9% are lived in by their owners, at a median value of $279,200.

Haywood mails bills in late August or early September, and payment is expected in September. No interest builds through January 5. Past that date a 2% charge applies, and 3/4% is added each time a new month begins. Paying in September is the simplest way to avoid all of it, and an owner who already knows a sale is coming should pay early so the payoff figure is a clean zero.

Haywood County property tax calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Who owns a parcel is determined for the tax year
Late August to early SeptemberBills mailed to owners
SeptemberTaxes due
January 5Last day without interest
After January 52% charge, then 3/4% monthly
MarchUnpaid real estate taxes advertised with a fee added

A bill you cannot clear by January 5 may qualify for a fixed monthly payment, so ask Collections. State law on interest is G.S. 105-360.

Options are the county website, the phone line at 1-877-729-8290, the mail, a dropbox outside the courthouse, and cash at the Collections counter. An outside processor adds 3% to card payments, online or by phone, and 2% to e-checks.

  • Put only checks and money orders in the dropbox, never cash.
  • Use the mailing address printed on your bill. The lockbox is now PO Box 96270, Charlotte. A returned payment can be resent to the Waynesville office in its original envelope, which keeps the first postmark.
  • Lenders and escrow companies get no bill from the county, so give your copy to the servicer if it pays your tax.

sections.h2: Why was the revaluation moved to 2027?
sections.html:
After Hurricane Helene, Haywood pushed its reappraisal back two years, from 2025 to January 1, 2027, after confirming with the state that the delay was allowed.

Until that date, most parcels keep the 2025 value. Exceptions are properties that changed through an addition, a remodel, new construction or flooding. The 2027 numbers will follow the market as it stands then, which could move a Waynesville or Maggie Valley assessment a long way.

The proposed 2027 schedule of values, standards and rules can be read at the assessor's second-floor office. Reappraisal must happen at least every eighth year under G.S. 105-286.

Use the county's Damage Report Form and deliver it to the assessor by hand, by post, or at personalproperty@haywoodcountync.gov. A flooded house should be reported before listing, so the assessment fits the house as it is now.

Disagreements over real property value are heard by a review board of five appointed members and one alternate, each on a one-year term. The assessor schedules its meetings as the need arises.

  • Ask to be heard before adjournment, as G.S. 105-322 requires.
  • The written decision arrives within a month after adjournment.
  • An appeal to the Property Tax Commission is due thirty days after the board mails its notice.

Before you go, gather whatever shows the damage or the value problem: photos, any repair estimates, and the Damage Report Form you already sent. Keep a copy of everything you submit. The board meets only when the assessor schedules it, so call 828-452-6734 early to ask when the next session is likely, rather than waiting until a sale is under contract.

Haywood owners can look at three state programs for a permanent residence, but only one may be claimed. Since 28.2% of residents are 65 or over, the age-based programs reach many homeowners. The application is Form AV-9, filed with the assessor.

  • Age 65 or older, or disabled, with 2026 income no higher than $38,800: half the value or $25,000 is shielded, whichever is more.
  • A veteran with a permanent, total service-connected disability gets $45,000 of value excluded.
  • The circuit breaker limits tax to 4.0% or 5.0% of income once you have lived in the home five years, and defers the balance.

The normal window is the January listing period, with applications taken through June 1. Any deferral ends when the house is transferred, so it shows up at closing.

A foreclosure can start the day after January 5 of the collection year, though the county says it acts only on owners who ignore notices or break a payment plan. First the collector can attach bank accounts, garnish wages or rents, or levy on personal property.

Two routes exist. In an in-rem foreclosure under G.S. 105-375, the Tax Department and County Attorney handle everything. In a mortgage-style case under G.S. 105-374, an outside attorney does. Sales are public auctions in front of the Haywood County Justice Center, as is and without warranty. The buyer puts down 20% and owes the balance at the end of the 10-day period and confirmation. Upset bids must exceed the last bid by 5%, at least $750, and are filed with the Clerk of Superior Court.

A sale does not wipe out the bill. The January 1 owner stays liable for that year, so the tax payoff is part of closing.

sections.h2: Steps for selling with taxes due
sections.html:
Start by phoning Collections for the clearing amount. Hand that number to the closing attorney, who will pay it from your proceeds. Anyone with a circuit breaker deferral should ask for that balance as well, since it comes due on transfer.

Storm-damaged sellers should file the damage form first, because buyers look at whether the assessment matches the house. A cash sale skips repairs and appraisals, yet the tax payoff is still settled at the table.

Closing date matters. Sell in October and the full year's bill still belongs to you, since ownership was fixed back on January 1. A fall closing can mean the bill arrives afterward, and it should go straight to the closing attorney. Leave it unpaid and interest begins after January 5, with the parcel advertised and a fee added by March.

faqs.q: When does interest start on Haywood County property tax?
faqs.a: Once January 5 passes. A 2% charge is added, then three-quarters of one percent more every month until the bill is paid.

faqs.q: Does Haywood County sell tax lien certificates?
faqs.a: No. North Carolina does not sell tax liens or certificates over the counter, and covering another person's delinquent bill gives you no ownership.

faqs.q: When is the next Haywood County revaluation?
faqs.a: It takes effect January 1, 2027, delayed from 2025 because of Hurricane Helene. Most parcels keep 2025 values until then.

faqs.q: I sold my house, so why did I get the tax bill?
faqs.a: Real property is taxed to whoever owned it on January 1, and a mid-year transfer leaves the seller responsible. Pay that year's tax at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I send storm damage reports?
faqs.a: To the Tax Assessor's Office at 215 N. Main Street, Suite 220, Waynesville, NC 28786, or by email to personalproperty@haywoodcountync.gov, using the Damage Report Form.
